original_question: Can Wigner distribution deconvolution be derived for arbitrary physically reasonable scanning patterns, rather than only full scans or simple scan grids, and what assumptions on the object are then necessary for recovery?
target_in_paper: Section 8.2, Question 8.5: "Can WDD be derived for arbitrary (reasonable) scanning patterns and which object assumptions are necessary?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact open problem in the paper: extending Wigner Distribution Deconvolution beyond the currently treated full-scan and grid-scan settings, and asking what assumptions on the object are needed for recovery once the scan pattern is generalized.
missing_details: The paper poses this in the discrete ptychographic setting, not as a general continuous-sampling question: f,w are vectors in C^n, with scan positions x drawn from a subset X of [n].
The relevant measurement model should be stated explicitly: I_{xi,x}=|F(f ⊙ S_x w)_{xi}|^2, where F is the discrete Fourier transform and S_x is the shift operator.
The statement is about deriving an analogue of the discrete WDD identity (26), whose standard form is available when all scan positions are used, i.e. X=[n].
The only non-full-scan case the paper says is currently understood is the grid scan X={sk : k in [n/s]}; this should be named explicitly rather than only saying "simple scan grids."

The paper's currently known recoverable object classes for grid scans are bandlimited objects and piecewise constant objects; these are the concrete examples behind your phrase "what assumptions on the object."
The paper says "arbitrary (reasonable) scanning patterns"; "physically reasonable" is close in spirit, but the official wording is slightly narrower and should be matched.

The role of the window/probe should be fixed in the statement: WDD is formulated for measurements generated by a probe w, while blind ptychography is mentioned only as motivation for why non-grid scans matter.

To stay paper-faithful, the refined question should remain in Section 8.2 and not drift into the later continuous sampled-STFT questions in Section 8.3, even though those are nearby and also concern subsampled measurements.

If the question is meant to be fully stand-alone, it should indicate that the goal is recovery via WDD from the measured data indexed by X, rather than a broad uniqueness question for arbitrary phase-retrieval models.
refined_question: In the discrete ptychographic setting of Section 8, let f,w be in C^n and let the measurements be I_{xi,x}=|F(f ⊙ S_x w)_{xi}|^2 for frequencies xi in [n] and scan positions x in a scan set X⊂[n]. Can one derive a Wigner Distribution Deconvolution formula analogous to the full-scan identity (26) for arbitrary reasonable scan patterns X—rather than only for the full scan X=[n] or the grid scan X={sk : k in [n/s]}—and, in that generalized setting, determine which structural assumptions on the object f are required for recovery via WDD (in the spirit of the currently known bandlimited or piecewise-constant cases for grid scans)?
justification: The draft is aimed at the open problem stated verbatim as Question 8.5 in Section 8.2. The surrounding context defines the continuous WDD identity (22)–(24), its discrete analogue (26), and explains that (26) requires the full scan X=[n], while the only established partial-scan case is the grid X={sk : k in [n/s]}, for which bandlimited or piecewise constant objects can be recovered. The paper then motivates more general scan patterns by noting that spiral scans and randomly perturbed grids are used in practice, especially because grid scans are undesirable in blind ptychography. This makes Question 8.5 the nearest official formulation and shows that your draft is close but omits the discrete signal model, the exact measurement/operator notation, the specific known scan classes, and the concrete object classes already mentioned by the paper. The later Section 8.3 questions concern continuous sampled STFT phase retrieval and are adjacent but not the same problem.
